title: Combinatorics & Modular Math — Depth Pass
relevance: High — second wave after CSES fact/invFact / stars-and-bars / Catalan; these are the CF Div2 C–D “count under constraints + mod inverse” drills that show up in harder OAs and blue→CM contests.
company_notes: FAANG/OA counting with modular pow as product over independent groups (Pocket Book, Alice and the List of Presents, Kyoya); contribution rewrite for sum of (max−min) over k-subsets (Max-Min Sums); complementary pair counting with no shared endpoint (Ball in Berland); expected product of a random pair via inverses (Sakurako’s Box).

phases.goal: Establish that the candidate spots depth-pass combo: a hidden rewrite whose answer is ways under a mod, not a named sequence.

must_hit.point: Depth-pass combo is recognized when the answer is ways mod 998244353/1e9+7 and constraints allow an O(n) pass after O(N) factorial precompute.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names modular ways plus fact/invFact precompute then a linear scan, not a closed Catalan/named formula.

must_hit.point: After named-sequence drills, the statement hides a rewrite: complementary count, per-index max/min contribution, product of independent column/type choices, or IE on sorted-key collisions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists complementary / contribution / independent product / sort-key IE as the rewrite family.

must_hit.point: Also flag depth-pass when the statement mixes counting with construction, binary-search paths, or gcd-constrained arrays.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions BS-path reconstruction or gcd-forced fill alongside modular counting.

probes: When do you treat a counting problem as depth-pass combo rather than a named sequence like Catalan?

hints.1: Look at the required output form and what the statement refuses to name.
hints.2: Ways mod 998244353 or 1e9+7 plus a rewrite (complement, contribution, independent product, IE) is the signal.
hints.3: Say: answer is ways mod 998244353/1e9+7, O(n) after O(N) fact precompute, or counting mixed with construction / binary-search paths / gcd arrays.

phases.goal: Show the candidate can choose the right rewrite—complement, contribution, sequential product, residue DP, sweep, hockey-stick, or IE.

must_hit.point: Prefer complementary counting total − invalid when invalids partition by a key (Ball in Berland: C(k,2) − ∑C(boy_c,2) − ∑C(girl_c,2); Number Of Permutations IE on sort-keys).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States total pairs/perms minus colliding partitions, possibly with +both for IE.

must_hit.point: Contribution / linearity: rewrite ∑_S f(S) as ∑_i a_i · (# subsets where i is max/min)—sort then a_i is max in C(i,K−1) subsets and min in C(n−1−i,K−1) (Max-Min Sums); same idea as digit place-value contribution.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts, multiplies each a_i by binomial counts of being max or min, not loops over all subsets.

must_hit.point: When type order is forced (last color/group fixed), answer is sequential product ∏ C(pref+c_i−1, c_i−1), not a single multinomial (Kyoya).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Places colors in forced order ending with last color; multiplies binomials of growing prefixes.

must_hit.point: Residue/constraint DP: pre-count values per residue class then DP the product (Ayoub mod 3); same pattern for ≤K adjacent same-color pairs ∑_{i=0}^{K} C(n−1,i)·m·(m−1)^{n−1−i}.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Builds residue frequencies then multiplies into dp[i][r], or sums the ≤K adjacent-pair formula.

must_hit.point: Sweep with live binomials: on each new segment opening with enough active, add C(active−1, k−1) (Rescue Nibel!); hockey-stick for grid-path rectangle sums via ∑ C(i+r,i)=C(n+r+1,n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts events and adds C(active−1,k−1), or reduces rectangle path sums with hockey-stick.

probes: Walk through how you would rewrite sum-of-f(S) over k-subsets, and when you would instead do total minus colliding pairs.

hints.1: Ask whether invalids share a key, or whether f(S) depends on who is max/min.
hints.2: Complement when partitions collide; contribution when each index’s max/min count is binomial after sort.
hints.3: Ball in Berland: C(k,2)−∑C(c,2); Max-Min Sums: a_i·C(i,K−1) / C(n−1−i,K−1); Kyoya: ∏ C(pref+c−1,c−1).

phases.goal: Confirm modular fact/invFact templates and the concrete modular formulas used on this ladder.

must_hit.point: Independent choices: per column count distinct letters and answer ∏ dist[j] mod 1e9+7 (Pocket Book); independent nonempty subsets give (2^n−1)^m (Alice and the List of Presents).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Implements product of column alphabets or modular pow of (2^n−1) across types.

must_hit.point: Sakurako’s Box: ∑_{i<j} a_i a_j / C(n,2) via ((∑a)^2−∑a^2)/2 · inv(C(n,2)), not nested pair loops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses sum and sum-of-squares plus modular inverse of C(n,2).

must_hit.point: Binary Search path counts: simulate BS on value x to get L larger and S smaller on the path, then C(n−x,L)·C(x−1,S)·(n−1−L−S)!.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Simulates the BS path, counts L and S, multiplies the two binomials by the remaining factorial.

must_hit.point: IE for two injections with forbidden equalities: P(M,N)^2 total, then ∑ (−1)^k C(N,k)·P(M−k,N−k)^2 (NEQ).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes alternating IE over k fixed equal positions with falling factorials.

probes: How do you implement the expected product of a random pair mod 1e9+7 without O(n^2) enumeration?

hints.1: Expand the pairwise product in terms of (∑a)^2 and ∑a^2.
hints.2: You need inv of C(n,2) after the algebraic identity.

phases.goal: Tie the approach to the stated constraint pattern: linear work after factorial precompute.

must_hit.point: Standard depth-pass shape: O(N) factorial (and invFact) precompute, then O(n) to answer.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States O(N) precompute of fact/invFact then an O(n) pass over the array or events.

must_hit.point: Close Tuples hard version upgrades to two pointers plus fact so each left endpoint’s C(#in [a_i, a_i+k], m−1) stays fast after sort.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts, two-pointers the window, answers with precomputed binomials—not per-query factorials from scratch.

probes: What complexity should you aim for once fact and invFact are precomputed?

hints.1: The research pattern line already states the target shape.
hints.2: Precompute factorials over the max N, then scan the n elements or events once.
hints.3: O(N) fact/invFact precompute, then O(n) to finish.

phases.goal: Surface the ladder’s easy-to-miss closed-form and structural traps.

must_hit.point: Jury Meeting: if max−second > 1 answer is 0; otherwise use an n! / (cnt_second+1)-style fact/inv count for unique-max adjacency.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Checks the max vs second gap before any factorial formula.

must_hit.point: Do not collapse Kyoya-style forced order into one multinomial; it is the sequential product ∏ C(pref+c_i−1, c_i−1) with last color fixed.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects a single multinomial and writes the prefix product of binomials.

must_hit.point: Gap placements (Shaass and Lights): multinomial of gap sizes times ∏ 2^{gap−1} only for internal gaps—not every gap.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Applies 2^{gap−1} only to internal gaps between already-on lights.

must_hit.point: Minimum number of steps: right-to-left, each a adds current b-count then doubles it (cnt_b = 2·cnt_b)—easy to get the modular chain order wrong.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Scans right-to-left, updates answer from cnt_b then doubles cnt_b on each a.

probes: What special-case check do you need before counting permutations with a unique maximum adjacency constraint?

hints.1: Compare the largest value to the second-largest.
hints.2: If they differ by more than one, no valid arrangement exists.
hints.3: If max−second > 1 → 0; else n! / (cnt_second+1) with fact/inv.

tradeoffs.topic: complementary total−invalid vs direct enumeration of valid pairs/perms
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Prefer total − invalid when invalids partition cleanly by a key (Ball in Berland C(k,2)−∑C(c,2); Number Of Permutations n! minus sorted-by-a/b plus both). Direct construction is harder when the bad set is the structured piece.

tradeoffs.topic: contribution/linearity on indices vs summing f(S) over all subsets
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Rewrite ∑_S f(S) as ∑_i a_i · (#S where i is max/min) after sorting (Max-Min Sums; same family as Bargain / Count The Blocks digit contribution) instead of enumerating subsets.

tradeoffs.topic: sequential placement product vs single multinomial
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When order of types is forced (last color fixed), use ∏ C(pref+c−1, c−1) (Kyoya)—not one multinomial over all color counts.

tradeoffs.topic: closed-form modular identity vs nested loops for expected pairwise product
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Sakurako’s Box forces ((∑a)^2−∑a^2)/2 · inv(C(n,2)) rather than nested loops over pairs.

gotchas.trap: Treating Kyoya / forced last-group placement as a single multinomial.
gotchas.correction: Last color is fixed; answer is the sequential product ∏ C(pref+c_i−1, c_i−1).

gotchas.trap: Skipping the Jury Meeting gap check and always emitting a factorial formula.
gotchas.correction: If max−second > 1 the answer is 0; only then apply the n! / (cnt_second+1)-style count.

gotchas.trap: Computing expected pairwise product with nested loops.
Applying 2^{gap−1} to every gap when placing lights.
gotchas.correction: Multinomial over gap sizes, and ∏ 2^{gap−1} only for internal gaps (Shaass and Lights).

gotchas.trap: Forgetting IE’s +both term when subtracting sorted-by-a and sorted-by-b permutations.
gotchas.correction: Number Of Permutations: n! − (#sorted by a) − (#sorted by b) + (#sorted by both).
